purpose: Define what happens when a citizen or official route supplies a document or record: receipt, identification, matching, validation, sufficiency feedback and return to the investigation.
core_principle: RECEIVE → IDENTIFY → MATCH → VALIDATE → ASSESS → FEEDBACK → CONTINUE
rules: A citizen-supplied document does not become an official record merely by submission.
Property and date matching are separate checks.
A document may be valid for one proposition but insufficient for another.
Conflicts are preserved and routed for review; they are not silently resolved.
Access restriction is recorded separately from evidential absence.
Privacy classification is applied before public exposure.
Validation results update the investigation but do not rewrite historical source records.
The citizen is told what was validated and what remains unresolved.
hard_stops: Never mark an item validated solely because it was uploaded.
Never infer property match from address or name alone where ambiguity exists.
Never infer legal effect from document existence alone.
Never expose restricted document content publicly.
Never report more certainty than the validation actually supports.
